content: 1. Omeprazole and Cannabidiol: Cannabidiol can increase the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting the hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. Consider reducing the dose of sensitive CYP2C19 substrates when co-administered with cannabidiol. 2. Omeprazole and Capecitabine: Omeprazole decreases the effects of capecitabine through an unknown mechanism. Retrospective data suggest that elevated gastric pH caused by proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) may impair the dissolution and/or absorption of capecitabine tablets. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Omeprazole and Carbamazepine: Carbamazepine decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Omeprazole and Carbonyl Iron: Omeprazole reduces the levels or effects of carbonyl iron by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Omeprazole and Cefpodoxime: Omeprazole decreases the effects of cefpodoxime by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Omeprazole and Cefuroxime: Omeprazole decreases the effects of cefuroxime by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Omeprazole and Cenobamate: Cenobamate decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, cenobamate increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. Consider dose reduction of CYP2C19 substrates when used concomitantly with cenobamate. 8. Omeprazole and Ciprofloxacin: Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of ciprofloxacin through an unknown mechanism. Co-administration with omeprazole slightly reduces the absorption of ciprofloxacin extended-release tablets by approximately 20%. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Omeprazole and Citalopram: Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of citalopram by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. The maximum recommended dose of citalopram for patients taking CYP2C19 inhibitors is 20 mg/day due to the risk of QT prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Omeprazole and Clobazam: Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of clobazam by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Dosage adjustment may be required as CYP2C19 inhibitors can increase exposure to N-desmethylclobazam, the active metabolite. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Omeprazole and Cobicistat: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Omeprazole and Conivaptan: Conivaptan increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Omeprazole and Crizotinib: Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of crizotinib by increasing gastric pH, which may reduce the solubility and bioavailability of crizotinib. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Omeprazole and Cyclosporine: Long-term use of PPIs like omeprazole may cause hypomagnesemia, which can increase the risk of cyclosporine toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Omeprazole and Dabrafenib: Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of dabrafenib by increasing gastric pH, potentially reducing its solubility and bioavailability. Dabrafenib also decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. 16. Omeprazole and Diazepam (Buccal and Intranasal): Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of diazepam by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism, which may decrease the rate of diazepam elimination and increase the risk of adverse reactions. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Omeprazole and Dichlorphenamide: Both omeprazole and dichlorphenamide decrease serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Omeprazole and Digoxin: Prolonged use of PPIs like omeprazole may cause hypomagnesemia, increasing the risk of digoxin toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Omeprazole and Efavirenz: Efavirenz has a dual effect on omeprazole, increasing its levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism and decreasing its levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Omeprazole and Elagolix: Elagolix increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism and decreases its levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. 21. Omeprazole and Eluxadoline: Omeprazole increases the levels of eluxadoline by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Due to incomplete information on eluxadoline metabolism, use caution when co-administering with strong CYP2C19 inhibitors. 22. Omeprazole and Escitalopram: Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of escitalopram by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Omeprazole and Eslicarbazepine Acetate: Eslicarbazepine acetate increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Omeprazole and Fluconazole: Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Omeprazole and Methotrexate: Omeprazole increases methotrexate levels by decreasing renal clearance. Temporary withdrawal of PPIs may be considered in some patients. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Omeprazole and Posaconazole: Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of posaconazole by increasing gastric pH. Conversely, posaconazole increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Omeprazole and Rifampin: Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Omeprazole and Ritonavir: Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Omeprazole and Rosé Hips: Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of rosé hips by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Omeprazole and Sparsentan: Sparsentan decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
